# Mingyang Liu (刘明杨)

> Mingyang Liu is a researcher in finance: PhD in Finance, Imperial College London (2026); Visiting Researcher at the Imperial Centre of Excellence in Quantitative Finance; on the 2026–27 academic job market (job market page: https://mingyangliu.org/jobmarket/). Research fields: empirical asset pricing, machine learning and big data in finance, financial econometrics. This site (https://mingyangliu.org, English with a Chinese mirror under /zh/) holds the five papers (The Ruler Matters is the job market paper), research in progress, a CV and a Projects section.

Name variants: Mingyang Liu, Liu Mingyang, Yang Liu (legal name, used in some listings), 刘明杨, 刘杨. Sole author of the five papers listed here; the corporate-bond working paper in progress is with Paolo Zaffaroni.

## Research

- [The Ruler Matters: Factor Exposures, Attribution, and Portfolio Risk](https://mingyangliu.org/research/the-ruler-matters.html) (job market paper): which stock positions an estimated factor-loading space represents, measured with the cross-sectional second moment of characteristics as the ruler, and what that implies for return attribution, hedging and portfolio risk. PDF: https://mingyangliu.org/assets/pdfs/The_Ruler_Matters.pdf
- [Same Forecasts, Different Portfolios: Factor Normalization and Regularization](https://mingyangliu.org/research/same-forecasts-different-portfolios.html): why two versions of one factor model with the same forecasts can hold different portfolios when a penalty on factor exposures is written in each version's own units, and what using the model's estimated intercept adds. PDF: https://mingyangliu.org/assets/pdfs/Same_Forecasts_Different_Portfolios.pdf
- [A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models](https://mingyangliu.org/research/geometric-framework.html): which ruler (a metric on characteristic space) should a factor model use to tell two combinations of firm characteristics apart? PDF: https://mingyangliu.org/assets/pdfs/Geometric_Framework_SSRN_7013178.pdf
- [Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference](https://mingyangliu.org/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html): why two factor models with the same fitted returns can split them differently, and how to report standard errors when the rule that splits them (the characteristic-space metric) is estimated. PDF: https://mingyangliu.org/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Space_Metrics_Main.pdf
- [Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts](https://mingyangliu.org/research/interpreting-pricing-errors.html): when one model reports a smaller alpha, did its factors explain more, or did the thing being explained change? PDF: https://mingyangliu.org/assets/pdfs/Interpreting_Estimated_Pricing_Errors.pdf
- Research in progress: *Exposure or Intercept? Identifying Corporate Bond Premia with No-Arbitrage IPCA*, with Paolo Zaffaroni (in preparation). See https://mingyangliu.org/research/#research-in-progress
- Research collaboration: An ongoing research collaboration with Prof. Semyon Malamud (EPFL and Swiss Finance Institute) on portfolio construction from linear out-of-sample return forecasts, complementing his work on nonlinear return prediction; the collaboration began after a seminar Mingyang Liu presented at EPFL in June 2026 at Malamud's invitation. Seminar announcement: https://memento.epfl.ch/event/no-arbitrage-factor-geometry-identification-in-hig/
- Presentations of the job market paper: University of Cambridge, Faculty of Economics, 4 November 2026 (invited; scheduled); EPFL, Lausanne, 16 June 2026 (invited seminar; precursor presented as No-Arbitrage Factor Geometry)
- [All research](https://mingyangliu.org/research/)


## Research Toolkit

- [Research Toolkit overview](https://mingyangliu.org/research-toolkit/): reusable research tools; each states its inputs, analyses, outputs and limits, and is demonstrated on an archived historical example.
- [Portfolio Risk Diagnostics: Return-State Behavior Profile](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/return-state-diagnostics.html): how a dated return stream behaved across benchmark-defined market states (conditional returns, downside beta, observation counts per state); demonstrated on an archived 2007–2025 backtest selected from several configurations in an earlier study; not actual trading and not an audited track record.
- [Macro Forecast Evaluation & Regime Diagnostics](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/forecast-evaluation.html): compares forecast models on matched pseudo-out-of-sample windows with documented look-ahead (RMSE, Diebold–Mariano tests, errors by state); demonstrated on archived UK services-inflation research (February 2026), not a forecasting service.


## Projects

- [Projects overview](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/): what has been built and tested for empirical finance research, with a status for each piece.
- [NA-IPCA toolkit](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/naipca-toolkit.html): two Python packages for IPCA-family factor models (ruler construction and diagnostics; estimation with an audit record for every fit); code on request.
- [From forecast to portfolio](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/forecast-to-portfolio.html), [Same fit, different attribution](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/why-the-ruler-matters.html), [Building the ruler](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/building-the-ruler.html), [Strategy notes](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/strategy-notes.html): research notes with the figures behind the papers.
- [ISIF AI operating system](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/isif-ai-operating-system.html) (workflow design), [Teaching notes](https://mingyangliu.org/projects/teaching-notes.html) (Financial Statistics, shared for academic use).
